fields.meta_title: Spelling Quiz: Play 8 Words, Then Build Yours | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Play an 8-word spelling quiz with a dictionary source behind each answer, then build one for your class that saves every misspelling.
fields.h1: Build a Spelling Quiz That Shows Which Words to Reteach
fields.hero_description: Build a spelling quiz from your word list that grades each spelling and saves every miss to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Inside the Spelling Quiz Emergent Builds
fields.features_subheading: Emergent writes the questions from your list. The app grades every letter and keeps each attempt, wrong spellings included.
fields.feature_1:
Three question formats from one word list

Paste this week's words and Emergent drafts a question for each. Students pick the right spelling from four, type the word from a short clue, or find the misspelled word.
fields.feature_2:
Typed words graded letter for letter

A typed answer counts only when every letter matches, so recieve is marked wrong. At the end, each student sees a score and the right spelling of each word they missed.
fields.feature_3:
The misspelling saved as it was typed

Every attempt is stored in a database you own, with the student, the word, and the spelling they entered. Seeing seperate typed by six students says more than a red mark.
fields.feature_4:
One word per screen for young spellers

Kids get one word per screen on a tablet or phone, with a large text box and a progress bar. A 15-word pretest fits into the first ten minutes of a Monday spelling lesson.
fields.feature_5:
Emails to parents, alerts to teachers

Email each parent the words their child missed, or post a class summary to a teacher's Slack channel. A reminder can reach anyone who has not taken Friday's spelling test.
fields.feature_6:
Your school's domain, your code

Run the quiz on your own domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep it for next year.
fields.why_title: Why Build a Spelling Quiz on Emergent?
fields.why_description: Each misspelling lands in a table you own, with no response cap when a whole grade takes the test. A prompt loads next week's list.

fields.tab_content_1:
Practice lists hold only the words each child missed

Every Monday, 48 third graders in 2 classes at Pellbridge Elementary take a 15-word pretest on a tablet. Each child's practice list holds only the words they missed, and Friday's test uses the full list again. This week, 7 of 48 spelled all 15 on Monday, and 29 of 48 did on Friday.
fields.tab_content_2:
From 18 club members, 4 qualify for the district bee

The Duskmoor Middle School spelling bee club has 18 members, who practice in 25-word rounds. Each word shows up as a definition and a sentence with a blank, and the student types it, so one wrong letter marks it wrong. After 3 rounds, the 4 top scorers qualified for the district bee, led by Isla Lunden with 24 of 25.
fields.tab_content_3:
Of 27 fifth graders, 14 missed the doubled consonants

Ms. Penry's class of 27 fifth graders at Bellcroft Elementary takes a 20-word quiz in which every word is tagged with the spelling rule it tests. Sorted by rule, the misses showed that 14 of 27 students got at least one doubled consonant wrong, as in beginning or occurred. That rule became next week's mini-lesson.
fields.tab_content_4:
Every score of 17 or better emails the recruiter

Front-desk applicants at Ozwell Staffing take a 20-word spelling check of office words such as receive, schedule, and separate. A score of 17 or more passes, and the recruiter gets an email with the applicant's name and score. Last month, 41 of 64 applicants passed and moved to a phone interview the same week.

plan.angle: Every result in the top 10 is a spelling quiz to take (Merriam-Webster's Spell It, SpellQuiz, Britannica, Studiosity, EnglishClub, Fact Monster) and only ESL Desk offers a basic builder. This page gives the searcher both: an 8-word pick-the-right-spelling quiz to play on the page, with a dictionary source behind each answer, then four spelling quizzes a teacher, a club coach and a recruiter run as their own app, each saving every typed or chosen spelling to a table that shows which words and which rules to teach again.
